newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Infrastructure to get 11 pct of Loy Yang A.
newsitem.headline: Infrastructure to get 11 pct of Loy Yang A.

text.p: Infrastructure Trust of Australia said on Tuesday it had purchased for A$160 million 11 percent of the equity in Victoria's Loy Yang A power station.

Infrastructure Trust said its securities would be reinstated to quotation on the Australian Stock Exchange, after the Victorian Government announced that the Horizon Energy consortium had won the bidding for the Loy Yang A power station for A$4.746 billion plus A$109 million of liabilities.
The Horizon consortium includes U.S. utilities NRG Energy Inc and CMS Energy Corp, Macquarie Bank Ltd Infrastructure Trust.
Infrastructure Trust, which requested suspension prior to the start of trade, quickly rose 11 cents to A$1.38 after its reinstatement.

Macquarie Infrastructure Investment Management Ltd (MIIML), which manages the Trust, said it had been reviewing a number of projects in infrastructure sectors since its listing on December 16 last year.

"The investment in Loy Yang A is a significant transaction for ITA, not only in terms of size but also because it diversifies ITA's stable of infrastructure assets in New South Wales and Victoria," MIIML managing director John Caldon said.
Infrastructure Trust said Loy Yang A had by far the cheapest operating costs of any coal fired generator in Australia, and was well placed to compete in a national electricity market.

CMS said earlier that 77 percent of the acquisition would be project financed by a consortium of banks coordinated by Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd's ANZ Investment Bank (ANZIB), with the remaining 23 percent comprised of partner equity.
